findings.consequence: An accepted socket location can expose the authenticated operator channel to an untrusted validator running under the supported same-UID arrangement.
findings.evidence: Counterexample: select runtimeUid/operatorUid 1000 and a socket under /usr/local/lib/work-engine/operator, with that directory owned by UID1000 and mode0700 and root-owned, non-writable ancestors. check_socket_parent accepts this layout. workspace-publication/src/custody.rs:446-493 exposes the entire /usr tree through --ro-bind without changing the host credential to a distinct UID. Read-only filesystem exposure does not prevent connecting to a pathname Unix socket; custody.rs:418-419 explicitly recognizes that distinction. The completion socket therefore remains reachable from the validator. publication_ingress.rs:4-13 authenticates only the connected UID, so such a descendant can submit operator commands using known record references, for example revoke_from_peer at publication.rs:490-503. It can queue the request during validation for processing afterward. This is a source-derived counterexample, not an executed exploit.
findings.remediation: Reject socket locations exposed by the actual reviewer/validator mount grants, including /usr, or explicitly mask the socket and its containing authority directory in every untrusted descendant. Preserve real peer authentication. Add a regression covering this otherwise-valid private-directory layout and an independently observed confined-descendant connection denial.

findings.consequence: A single client transport failure terminates the production completion server and leaves a socket pathname that prevents a subsequent cold start until operator cleanup.
findings.evidence: serve_connection_checked returns an error for an oversized request, read timeout or failed response write (work-engine-completion-host/src/lib.rs:296-304,327-328). The new listener loop propagates that connection-local error with '?'. A client sending 1,048,577 bytes therefore exits the entire host before request decoding; a client disconnecting before its response can do the same after command execution. The socket is intentionally retained, and the next UnixListener::bind at completion.rs:372 fails on the existing pathname.
findings.remediation: Handle bounded client framing/read/write failures at the connection boundary and continue accepting subsequent peers. Keep deployment-authority failures fail-closed and preserve uncertain command outcomes without replay. Add a listener regression showing that an oversized or disconnected client does not prevent a following valid request.
